headline: On Monday, November 16, 2026, U.S. stocks closed sharply lower, with technology shares leading a broad sell-off.
summary: On Monday, November 16, 2026, U.S. stocks closed sharply lower, with technology shares leading a broad sell-off. The decline marked the third consecutive losing session for the S&P 500 and the worst day for major indexes since the post-election turbulence earlier in the month. Residual uncertainty surrounding Nvidia’s leadership change, combined with caution ahead of the company’s earnings, weighed heavily on the market.

us_equities.breadth: Market breadth was weak, with decliners far outnumbering advancers.
us_equities.sectors: Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sectors ended lower.

bonds.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield eased slightly, closing near 5.12% (down a few basis points). Yields pulled back after their recent climb on inflation concerns.

commodities.summary: Oil prices declined. WTI crude fell roughly 0.4% to the mid-$85 range. Gold was little changed to modestly higher.
commodities.oil: WTI crude fell roughly 0.4% to the mid-$85 range.
commodities.gold: Gold was little changed to modestly higher.

currencies.summary: The U.S. dollar strengthened, reaching a multi-month high. Volatility rose, with the VIX climbing above 22.

global_markets.summary: Asian markets were weaker, with notable declines in Japan, China, and South Korea. European equities also pulled back from recent highs.

key_drivers.title: Nvidia and AI/tech pressure
key_drivers.text: Nvidia shares fell about 4% as investors remained cautious following last week’s resignation of CEO Jensen Huang and ahead of the company’s earnings report (due after the close on Tuesday). Related semiconductor and AI-linked stocks also declined.

key_drivers.title: Broader risk-off tone
key_drivers.text: The sell-off extended beyond chips into other growth and cyclical areas. Defensive groups such as consumer staples provided some offset.

key_drivers.title: Upcoming catalysts
key_drivers.text: Markets focused on Nvidia’s results and the anticipated Anthropic IPO later in the week, amplifying caution around the AI trade.

key_drivers.title: Yields and oil
key_drivers.text: A modest retreat in Treasury yields and lower oil prices failed to support equities.

key_drivers.title: Technical context
key_drivers.text: The session represented the largest one-day percentage declines for the major averages since the early-November post-election move.

overall_tone: Risk-off and tech-led weakness. The market opened the week under pressure from ongoing Nvidia-related uncertainty and position-trimming ahead of key AI-sector events, resulting in a broad decline that erased a portion of the prior week’s rebound.

headline: On Friday, November 13, 2026, U.S. stocks finished mixed, with the Dow eking out a small gain while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined.
summary: On Friday, November 13, 2026, U.S. stocks finished mixed, with the Dow eking out a small gain while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined. Technology and semiconductor shares remained under pressure following the prior day’s leadership upheaval at Nvidia, outweighing a cooler-than-expected monthly reading on wholesale inflation. Despite the pullback, major indexes posted solid weekly gains, snapping multi-week losing streaks.

us_equities.breadth: Breadth was mixed, and the session saw early weakness that only partially recovered.

bonds.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield rose, closing near 5.15% (up roughly 5 basis points on the day). Yields have climbed notably over the past week amid sticky inflation data and expectations for further Federal Reserve rate increases.

commodities.summary: Oil prices were little changed to modestly higher. WTI crude settled in the high $88s per barrel range after the prior session’s rebound tied to Middle East developments. Energy shares held up relatively well.
commodities.oil: WTI crude settled in the high $88s per barrel range after the prior session’s rebound tied to Middle East developments.

currencies.summary: The dollar remained firm against a backdrop of elevated U.S. yields and rate-hike expectations. Volatility (VIX) edged higher.

global_markets.summary: European markets were mixed. Broader global sentiment reflected ongoing caution around U.S. tech leadership uncertainty and inflation data.

key_drivers.title: Continued Nvidia/tech pressure
key_drivers.text: Shares of Nvidia and related semiconductor names stayed under pressure a day after the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang. The uncertainty contributed to broader weakness in high-growth technology stocks.

key_drivers.title: October Producer Price Index
key_drivers.text: Wholesale prices rose 0.3% month-over-month (slightly below the 0.4% consensus), but the year-over-year rate accelerated to 6.5%, the highest since November 2022. Core measures also remained elevated. The data did little to alter expectations for at least a 25-basis-point Fed hike in December.

key_drivers.title: Weekly rebound
key_drivers.text: Despite Friday’s softness, the S&P 500 gained about 2.5% for the week, the Nasdaq roughly 2.3%, and the Dow about 2.1%. This marked the first winning week for the major indexes in several weeks.

key_drivers.title: Sector rotation
key_drivers.text: Defensive areas such as consumer staples and energy outperformed, while technology and some cyclical groups lagged.

key_drivers.title: Rate and inflation backdrop
key_drivers.text: Elevated and rising Treasury yields continued to weigh on rate-sensitive and growth-oriented equities.

overall_tone: Mixed and cautious. The market absorbed residual Nvidia-related volatility and a sticky PPI print without a sharp sell-off, while locking in meaningful weekly gains after a turbulent stretch. Investors remain focused on the path of inflation and Federal Reserve policy heading into December.

headline: On Thursday, November 12, 2026, U.S. stocks closed modestly lower after absorbing sharp early swings in Nvidia and a rise in oil prices.
summary: On Thursday, November 12, 2026, U.S. stocks closed modestly lower after absorbing sharp early swings in Nvidia and a rise in oil prices. The major averages opened down nearly 1% but recovered most of the losses to finish with relatively contained declines.

us_equities.sectors: Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sectors ended lower.

bonds.summary: Treasury yields remained elevated near recent highs following the prior session’s inflation-driven moves, with the 10-year still hovering around the 5% area in the broader recent context.

commodities.summary: Oil prices climbed after comments from President Trump indicating reduced interest in a deal with Iran, renewing supply concerns. Energy shares benefited relatively.

currencies.summary: The dollar held firm amid ongoing rate expectations. Volatility was elevated early but moderated as the market recovered from session lows.

global_markets.summary: International equities were mixed, with some pressure from the U.S. tech volatility and oil moves.

key_drivers.title: Nvidia leadership change
key_drivers.text: Shares initially plunged as much as 14% on the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang (CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO). The stock recovered a substantial portion of the decline, limiting broader index damage. Other AI chip names held up better.

key_drivers.title: Oil rebound
key_drivers.text: Crude rose on renewed geopolitical concerns after the administration signaled less interest in an Iran deal, supporting energy stocks.

key_drivers.title: Risk absorption
key_drivers.text: The market opened sharply lower but clawed back most losses, showing resilience after the prior day’s AI-driven rebound.

key_drivers.title: Sector rotation
key_drivers.text: Energy gained while cyclical and materials names lagged; technology was mixed due to Nvidia’s weight.

key_drivers.title: Ongoing rate backdrop
key_drivers.text: Elevated Treasury yields and Fed hike expectations continued to influence sentiment, though the bond market had been closed the previous day for Veterans Day.

overall_tone: Contained pullback. The market demonstrated resilience by recovering from early losses driven by Nvidia’s leadership news and oil volatility, finishing with only modest declines after Wednesday’s stronger session.

headline: On Wednesday, November 11, 2026 (Veterans Day), U.S. stocks advanced, led by a rebound in artificial intelligence and technology shares.
summary: On Wednesday, November 11, 2026 (Veterans Day), U.S. stocks advanced, led by a rebound in artificial intelligence and technology shares. The stock market traded normal hours while the U.S. bond market was closed for the federal holiday.

bonds.summary: The U.S. bond market was closed for Veterans Day (SIFMA holiday recommendation). Yields had risen the prior day on hotter inflation data and remained elevated near the 5% area on the 10-year heading into the holiday.

commodities.summary: Oil prices rose. Gold was relatively stable to softer in the broader recent context of higher yields.
commodities.gold: Gold was relatively stable to softer in the broader recent context of higher yields.

currencies.summary: The dollar held firm. Volatility measures declined as risk appetite improved in equities.

global_markets.summary: International markets were mixed to positive, with technology and growth-oriented names following the U.S. lead.

key_drivers.title: CoreWeave earnings
key_drivers.text: The AI cloud/infrastructure company reported stronger-than-expected results and raised guidance, while addressing funding and profitability concerns. Shares surged and lifted related AI and semiconductor names.

key_drivers.title: AI/tech rebound
key_drivers.text: Nvidia recovered ground after recent sharp declines tied to company-specific news. Broader chip and AI infrastructure stocks participated in the rally.

key_drivers.title: Holiday trading
key_drivers.text: Stocks traded normally while bonds were shut, limiting some rate-related price discovery.

key_drivers.title: Post-volatility recovery
key_drivers.text: The session extended the rebound from the prior week’s AI-regulation and midterm-related selling, with improved sentiment around AI spending sustainability.

key_drivers.title: Oil firmness
key_drivers.text: Crude prices increased, providing a mild tailwind for energy-related areas.

overall_tone: Constructive risk-on session. Strong results from CoreWeave helped restore confidence in the AI trade, driving technology leadership and allowing major indices to claw back more of the recent losses even as the bond market observed the holiday.
